## Defect
Fidelity gaps between `make test` and the retained test action, found while building the runner:
- The policy must name every case. `scripts/litai_retained_author.py` derives 483 cases from make's database for `test-impl`/`test` prerequisites (`test-*` plus `shadow-check`) and my `run-cases` runs each as `make <case>`. The framework has no per-case report model beyond what `run-cases` writes.
- `make test` swaps `bin/nanoc` to `nanoc_c`, passes `NANOLANG_COMPILER`, bounds the run with `TEST_TIMEOUT` (1800s) and restores the bootstrap link. `run-cases` reproduces this (three-case trial passed), but one case, `shadow-check`, failed once with make's default `CMD_TIMEOUT=600` killing the self-hosted `nanoisa_emitter` compile on a host with load average 216–261. `run-cases` now passes `CMD_TIMEOUT=1800`, a deliberate deviation from `make test`.
- Action timeouts are capped at 86,400s, and the 483-case action is set to that cap.
- The self-hosted compile is CPU-heavy (about 356s unloaded), so load-induced timeouts will read as test failures.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `run-cases` equivalence with `make test` is demonstrated on the full case list, not three cases.
- [ ] The test action is split below the 24h cap, or the cap is shown to be sufficient on a quiet host.
- [ ] Load-induced timeouts are distinguishable from test failures in the report.
- [ ] The independent acceptance policy (`verification/retained-project-acceptance.json`) is reviewed. It holds four golden-output cases of built executables (`nano_vm --bogus`, `nanoisa_emitter`, `parser`, `nvm2c`) recorded from the binary under test, so it is a golden check, not an independent oracle.
title: Retained test action fidelity: make test equivalence, timeouts and acceptance-policy review

## Defect
The retained path has no native-unit, header-closure or output-ownership model. I filled the gap with two nanolang scripts, and neither is a framework contract:
- `scripts/litai_native_inventory.py` parses `make -n -B build` into 220 compile units, 4 links, 1 archive, 4 generator invocations and 63 `src_nano/*.nano` sources, with header closure from `cc -MM -MG`. - `scripts/litai_retained_author.py` writes the profile, 483-case test policy, acceptance policy and the 89,420-file manifest.

## Operational costs observed
- Any edit under `docs/` (a manifest root) means rehashing the manifest, about 13 minutes.
- The authority-review marker in `docs/literate-ai/ADOPTION.md` depends on authority state. Editing that doc changes the required marker, so finalising text, marker and manifest takes several cycles.
- Manifest discovery aborts when a root ancestor's device number changes mid-walk (`reason=identity; name='/'`). It happened once and a rerun succeeded.
- Ignored build products under retained roots (`modules/index.json`, `tests/__pycache__`, `tests/actor/*.dSYM`) must be removed first, because the framework walks the filesystem.
- Reinstalling litai invalidates the pinned distribution (`rebuild.standard_distribution_mismatch`) until `rebind-standard` is re-applied.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A native-unit/closure model is available in the framework, or the inventory above is promoted to a reviewed, tested contract.
- [ ] Manifest generation is incremental, or docs are excluded from the retained roots by an accepted rule.
- [ ] The authority marker no longer needs repeated regeneration.
- [ ] Linux inventory exists, and the unparsed archive steps and self-hosted stages are covered.

Part of #1039 (LITAI-001.3/.4). Evidence is on branch `feat/litai-full-conversion`.

## Defect
`litai build --allow-host-execution` on the reviewed retained plan (`sha256:3923731e…dff1`, litai 1.4.0 git `22062a72`) refuses before any build or test case runs:

`retained.dependencies.observation-rejected: toolchain command …/literate/retained/tools/build-native is not a direct Mach-O binary`

The framework accepts a toolchain command only as a hashed in-tree Mach-O member. My three tools (`build-native`, `host-make`, `run-cases`) are scripts that delegate to the host `make`, `cc` and SDK. A compiled launcher would pass the check but would still leave the real toolchain unverified, so I did not add one.

## Consequence
There is no way on litai 1.4.0 to express "build with the installed Xcode toolchain" with verified provenance. The retained execution path cannot produce a receipt for nanolang as built today.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Decide the toolchain model: vendored hashed binaries, or a framework-supported host-toolchain identity (compiler path, hash, SDK, `xcrun` result).
- [ ] The decision is implemented or the framework gap is accepted upstream (related: jordanhubbard/literate-ai #22, #74).
- [ ] `--allow-host-execution` runs the build action to completion and records the toolchain identity in the receipt.

No code change to nanolang is implied until the model is chosen.
title: Retained execution rejects script tools: no verified host-toolchain model on Darwin
